h1: How Should a Push-Up Bra Fit?
keywords: how should a push up bra fit
how should push up bras fit
how are push up bras supposed to fit
how is a push up bra supposed to fit
answer: A push-up bra fits when the band is snug and level on the loosest hook, the padding sits below and beside your breast so it lifts it up and in, the top edge lies flat with no gap or harsh overflow, and the center gore rests against your breastbone without digging in.
intro: A push-up bra is still a bra first. The band, wire and gore checks are the same as for any underwire, but the padding takes up room inside the cup, so the cup has to be judged differently. Some fullness above the neckline is the point; spilling out at the sides or a ridge cutting across the breast is not. Fasten it on the loosest hook, lean forward to settle your breasts into the cups, then stand up and check.

checklist.good: Snug and level around your ribcage, with room for about two fingers under the back. It shouldn't shift when you lift your arms.
checklist.tooTight: It digs in and leaves deep marks, or you feel the padding pressing hard because the whole bra is compressed.
checklist.tooLoose: The back rides up, letting the cups drop so the padding no longer lifts. Push-up bras need a firm band to work at all.

checklist.good: The padding sits at the bottom and outer sides of the cup, under your breast, and lifts it toward the center. Your breast fills the space above the padding smoothly.
checklist.tooTight: Breast tissue bulges well over the top edge or out at the sides, or you can see a hard line where the cup edge cuts across.
checklist.tooLoose: The top of the cup gapes or wrinkles, or the cup stands away from your breast when you lean forward.

checklist.good: The wire traces the fold under your breast and ends on your ribs at the side, behind the breast tissue.
checklist.tooTight: The wire sits on breast tissue at the side or under the arm, which often means the cup is too small.
checklist.tooLoose: The wire sits away from your body or slides upward onto the breast when you move.

checklist.good: Rests flat against your breastbone. Many push-up styles have a low, short gore, so it may sit lower than on a full-cup bra.
checklist.tooTight: The gore stabs or presses into your breastbone, or the wires overlap tissue at the center.
checklist.tooLoose: The gore floats off your chest, so the lift and cleavage don't line up in the middle.

checklist.good: Adjusted so they stay put with a finger's width of give. They help angle the lift but shouldn't be doing the lifting.
checklist.tooTight: They dig into your shoulders or pull the back of the band up, often because they're compensating for a loose band.
checklist.tooLoose: They slide off your shoulders and the cups tip forward.

checklist.good: The top edge lies flat against your breast. A smooth curve of fullness above it is expected.
checklist.tooTight: The edge cuts in and creates a double-bubble line visible under clothes.
checklist.tooLoose: The edge stands away from your chest, especially at the inner top of the cup.

variations.heading: Light, medium and maximum push-up
variations.intro: The amount of padding changes how much room the cup has for you. The more padding, the more likely you need to try different sizes.

items.name: Light or graduated padding
items.text: A thin layer of foam that gets slightly thicker toward the bottom. Usually fits the same size as your everyday underwire bra and gives a natural lift.

items.name: Medium or removable pads
items.text: Inserts or thicker graduated foam. If the cup feels overfull with the pads in, try removing them before you size up. Removable pads also let you balance a size difference between breasts by taking out the pad on the fuller side.

items.name: Maximum or double push-up
items.text: Thick padding that takes up a lot of the cup. Some people go up one cup size to make room. Check that your breast still sits inside the cup at the sides, not just pushed out over the top.

items.name: Plunge push-up
items.text: A deep center for low-cut necklines. The gore is short and set low, so judge fit by the band and side wires rather than whether the gore is pressed tight.

items.name: Wireless push-up
items.text: Relies on molded foam and a snug band. It gives a softer lift, and the band has to be firm because there's no wire anchoring the cups.

measure.heading: How to find your push-up bra size
measure.intro: Start from your regular bra size, then adjust for padding. Measure with a soft tape over an unpadded bra or none.
steps: Measure snugly around your ribcage directly under your breasts, tape level, after exhaling. Round to the nearest even number for your band size. Some brands still add 4 in (or 5 in for odd numbers); check the brand's chart.
Measure loosely around the fullest part of your bust, keeping the tape level across your back.
Subtract the band size from the bust measurement. Each inch is one cup: 1 in is A, 2 in is B, 3 in is C, 4 in is D, 5 in is DD.
Try your measured size first. If the padding leaves your breasts bulging over the top edge, try one cup larger on the same band.
If the cups fit but the band doesn't, switch to a sister size (down a band and up a cup, or the reverse) instead of changing only one number.
measure.tip: Shop for a push-up bra with the top you plan to wear it under. A neckline that flatters with a moderate push-up can look overfilled with a maximum one.

sizeTable.caption: Bra band size conversions
sizeTable.note: EU bands are underbust centimeters rounded to the nearest 5; French bands add 15. Cup letters match between US and UK up to DD and then diverge, so check each brand's chart above a D.

problems.problem: Breasts spill out over the top of the cups
problems.fix: Some fullness is expected, but a hard ridge means too little room. Go up a cup, remove inserts if they come out, or choose a lighter push-up level.

problems.problem: The cups gape at the top
problems.fix: The padding is pushing the cup away from you or the cup is too big. Try one cup smaller, or a plunge or balconette cut that sits lower on the breast.

problems.problem: The lift disappears after an hour
problems.fix: The band has loosened or was too big to begin with. Move to a tighter hook or try a smaller band with a larger cup (sister size).

problems.problem: Wires dig in under the arms
problems.fix: Thick padding can push wires backward. Try a cup size up so the wire sits on your ribs, or a style with shorter side wires.

problems.problem: One side looks fuller than the other
problems.fix: Fit the larger breast, then use a removable pad on the smaller side only. Small differences between breasts are very common.

extra.heading: Sister sizes for push-up bras
extra.body: Because padding changes the cup volume, you may land between sizes. Sister sizes keep cup volume about the same while changing the band: 34B, 32C and 36A are sisters, as are 34C, 32D and 36B. If the band feels loose but the cups are right, go down a band and up a cup. If the cups are right but the band is tight, go up a band and down a cup.

extra.heading: Caring for padded cups
extra.body: Hand-wash or use a mesh bag on a gentle cycle and lay flat to dry. Fold a molded bra at the band, never cup inside cup, because creased foam won't sit smoothly again. Replace a push-up bra when the foam dents, the band loses grip, or the lift has visibly dropped.

picks.label: Push-up bra with removable pads
picks.why: Lets you adjust the amount of lift, or balance two different-sized breasts, without changing size.
picks.query: push up bra removable pads underwire

picks.label: Plunge push-up bra
picks.why: A low center gore for V-necks and wrap tops; it often suits close-set breasts.
picks.query: plunge push up bra deep v

picks.label: Wireless push-up bra
picks.why: A softer option for everyday wear if underwires feel uncomfortable. Choose one with a firm band.

faqs.q: Should you size up in a push-up bra?
faqs.a: Not usually for light or medium padding. With maximum or double push-up padding, some people need one cup larger on the same band to keep their breasts inside the cup.

faqs.q: Is it normal for a push-up bra to feel tight?
faqs.a: The band should feel firm but not painful, and the cups should feel snug. Deep marks, pinching or restricted breathing mean the size is wrong.

faqs.q: How much cleavage should a push-up bra show?
faqs.a: A smooth curve above the cup edge is the intended look. A hard line or a bulge that looks like a second breast above the cup means the cup is too small.

faqs.q: Why does my push-up bra gap at the top?
faqs.a: The cup is too big, or the padding is pushing it off a breast shape it doesn't suit. Try one cup smaller or a lower-cut style such as a balconette or plunge.

faqs.q: Can you wear a push-up bra every day?
faqs.a: Yes, if it fits well. Many people find a light or graduated push-up comfortable all day, and keep heavier padding for occasional outfits.
